topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, outlining the lecture structure and intended learning outcomes on cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetic mechanisms, environmental exposures, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce fundamental concepts of cancer causation, contrasting intrinsic and stochastic mutation processes with environmental exposures and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens drive cancer development, using Burkitt lymphoma as an illustrative case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical compounds undergo cellular metabolism to form reactive intermediates and direct DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanisms of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental stage interact with initiation to drive malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying, testing, and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify mutational signatures, test carcinogenicity, and weigh exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, summarizing the lecture's key themes regarding environmental cancer risk and benefit analysis.
